_how: Every push: bump version, add a new entry at the top of history. 'notes' is for installs older than 2026.11.05.9, whose updater only reads this list; keep it as all history notes. 'tour' lists the tutorial step ids (TOUR_STEPS in viewer/index.html) this release added or changed, for the 'what's new' tour; run check_tour.py before pushing.
notes: Long team jobs no longer get cut off at 45 minutes and quietly started again from scratch. A job now stops only if nobody on the team has done anything for 20 minutes (it looks stuck), or after 4 hours; you hear about it straight away, and saying "carry on" picks up where the team left off.

Answers in the main chat are now laid out to be easy to read: short paragraphs, bullet points, bold lead-ins and headings for longer replies, instead of one long run of text. Team reports in the answer card look the same way. What he says aloud is unchanged.
The Team Inbox and Deliverables cards and the To file counts now update by themselves when the team files or adds something, so you no longer see files that have already gone.
In the office view, empty charging pads show the Carbonhalo mark; when a bot stands on one, it glows as a solid circle.
The Logo galaxy view is now a thicker 3D mark that slowly turns like a coin while spinning like the Halo emblem, without the tangle of note-to-note lines hiding the petals.
Fixed: the desktop shortcut could keep showing the old Jarvis picture. It now shows the Halo mark.
The desktop and Start menu shortcut is now called Halo, with the Halo icon. It renames itself the first time Halo starts after this update.

Jarvis is now Halo (H.A.L.O.). The ring on the right is replaced by the Carbonhalo mark: it draws itself, fills and sends out soft pulses while waiting, goes pale and ripples while listening, spins with a chasing petal while thinking, and spins while he talks. New icon on the desktop shortcut too. He still answers if you call him Jarvis, and your settings, chats and shortcut keep working as before.
Settings > Tutorial > What's new always shows something now: what changed since your last tour, or the latest update's steps if you've seen them all.

The tutorial now shows how to format notes and how to dictate one: say "new heading", "bullet point" or "new task" as you talk, then Tidy up to sort it. Tutorial cards also move out of the way when they would cover the button they're pointing at.

Notes now look formatted while you write: bold shows as bold, headings as headings, and bullets, numbered lists and tick-box tasks as real lists. Use the buttons, or type "## ", "- ", "1. " or "[] " at the start of a line. You can also rename a saved note: change its name and press Save.

Notes can now have headings, bullets, numbered lists and tick-box tasks. Use the new formatting bar, or say "new paragraph", "bullet point", "number point", "new heading" or "new task" while dictating. Preview shows the note formatted. Tidy up (or "Tidy after dictating") lets Jarvis add the structure for you without changing your words. Dictation no longer wipes what you type while it listens.

Jarvis keeps running if whatever started him closes, for example the Claude Code window used to install or update him. Before, closing that window too soon could take Jarvis down with it ("site can't be reached").

Jarvis now finds notes by meaning, not just exact words: ask about "the truck dealership's risk meeting" and he finds the note called "governance session". Exact names still come first. It runs on your own computer (nothing is sent anywhere) and sets itself up in the background the first time, so it may take a few minutes after this update before it kicks in.
Settings no longer has a Jobs tab: everything it did is on the Jobs card on the left. Jobs in your daily brief open that job's page.

Jarvis now remembers. Your conversations with him are kept (across windows, days and restarts), he recalls older chats that match what you ask, he knows what the team has finished lately, and he keeps a list of facts to remember for good. Say "remember that..." or just correct him, and he notes it; when something changes, the newest wins.

New Jobs card on the left: click it and all your scheduled jobs open in the main window, with when each runs next, who does it and how the last run went. Click a job to see what it does and edit its instructions right there; the next run follows them.
Feedback now includes your name and Jarvis version, so Richie knows who sent it and which version you're on.
New Feedback button, bottom left beside Settings: tell Richie about a bug, an idea or a feature you'd like. The form opens in a small window and sends your name and Jarvis version with it.

Ask a question in a job's chat with Larry ("what is this for?", "has Felix finished?") and you get an answer in a few seconds, from what the team is doing right now, even while they wait for your approval. Instructions still go to Larry, and the chat tells you if he's paused waiting on you.
Approval cards now show the agent's reason, taken from what they last said, when they didn't give one.
"See what the team is doing" is now a single button: click it and the team window opens in the middle of the screen. The small arrow and the short list in the tray are gone.

Asking for more while Larry is working no longer starts a second Larry beside him: a correction or extra request from the main chat or any chat with Larry goes into the job he's already on, so two copies of the team can't overwrite each other's files.

Messages in a job's chat with Larry always run as team work: you can type while the job is running, and anything you send afterwards carries on the same thread, shows in the team window and reports back in that chat.

Jobs are announced once, as soon as they finish: Jarvis no longer waits for the galaxy to refresh, still announces a job that finished after the page reloaded, and says just who finished what (the full report is on screen).

Clicking a busy team member in the team window opens that job's chat with Larry, showing your request as sent and the progress live. It no longer opens an empty chat with the task typed in, which looked unsent and ran the job twice if sent.

New tutorial: Jarvis tells you what he can do for you, then shows you round every menu, the top bar, the team and Settings, step by step with made-up example data (your own notes are never shown or changed). It starts on a new install before his greeting; replay it any time from Settings > Tutorial, or say "give me a tour". After each update he offers to show you just what's new.

Updates are easier to spot: when a new version is out, a flashing "Update now" button appears at the top centre of the screen. Jarvis checks when it starts and once a day, and you can say "update yourself" to check straight away.
New Nucleus view (replaces Tree, in the View menu under the index): your notes form a ball that slowly swirls round a nucleus of projects, agents and folders.
"See what the team is doing" opens the team window again. The small arrow on its right shows or folds the short list in the tray.
Ask Jarvis to set up a job ("every Friday at 2pm, remind me what's still open"): he asks what he needs, then creates it. Say it again with changes and he updates the same job.
Settings > Jobs: each job's light pulses green while it's on, amber while it runs, red if its last run failed, and is grey when paused.
Pop-up windows, including the job editor, can be resized from the bottom-right corner and remember their size. The job editor no longer scrolls sideways.
Jarvis starts talking sooner: the spoken answer begins as soon as it's ready, while the written reply is still appearing on screen.
Project chat now takes files too: attach with the paperclip, paste with Ctrl+V or drop a file on the box, and it goes into the Team Inbox.
Settings > Jobs > Add a job offers a Weekly knowledge capture (Friday afternoon: turns the week's decisions and repeatable work into decision log entries, draft how-to guides and templates).

New 'Your tools' step: tick what you use (Outlook, Fireflies, Gmail and Google Calendar, Slack, monday.com) and Jarvis checks each one is connected. Existing installs see it once as a card. Anything you don't use is switched off, so the daily brief never waits on it.
Settings > Jobs > Add a job now offers a ready-made Weekly status update (Friday afternoon: what moved per client, what's overdue, what's next).
Ticking an action off in Jarvis now records the day it was done (date_closed).

Daily brief: the first time you open Jarvis each day, a card shows what's due, what's waiting for your decision, today's calendar, and what changed since last time (new email, finished jobs, notes, Team Inbox). Jarvis reads out a short summary instead of the usual greeting. Ask "show me my brief" to see it again.
Settings > Tools: the tools Jarvis and the team use (Claude Code, your notes, Outlook, Fireflies, and any you add), each with a Test button and a green or red light.

Settings > Jobs: schedule work for the team (every day, weekdays, weekly or every few hours), with Run now, Pause and a log. Jobs run while your computer is on; one missed while it was off runs once when Jarvis starts again.
The Logo view is back to the flat Carbonhalo mark.
The Logo view is now 3D: each petal of the mark has depth and a slight twist, and the connections arc around it. It opens at an angle and slowly turns so the depth shows.

Faster answers. Small talk and screen commands ("show my actions") now take about 3 seconds, and questions about your notes about half as long as before. Jarvis replies the moment the answer is ready instead of waiting for Claude to shut down.

Calendar and email questions are quicker: only those words go to Outlook, other connectors are left out of the request, and "what's on today" or "any new emails" is answered from the Outlook card when it's fresh.
New View menu under the zoom buttons: show the galaxy as Concentric, Rings, Spiral, Tree or Logo. Galaxy stays the default and your choice is remembered.

The 'Jarvis standing by' box is gone. Click 'See what the team is doing' and it opens up right there, showing each agent at work: project, task and what they're doing now. Click an agent to open their chat.
In project chat, clicking another project in the Projects list switches the chat to it. Anything you'd typed but not sent is kept for each project. Team chat does the same when you click an agent.
Add files to the Team Inbox from the main chat: click the paperclip, paste with Ctrl+V (screenshots too) or drop a file on the chat box. Jarvis is told about the file in your next question.
Spoken replies can now run to about 110 words, so Jarvis explains the answer and his reasoning, not just a verdict.
Microphone: tap it once to talk, tap again to pause. Your words stay in the box and nothing is sent until you press the arrow (or Enter). Tap the mic again to carry on.
Microphone: Jarvis no longer hears himself. While he speaks, the mic holds and picks up again when he finishes.
The team tray under the Jarvis emblem no longer flashes and is bigger. New 'See what the team is doing' window shows who is working on what, anything waiting for you, and what finished recently.
Galaxy labels are now white.
Team Inbox and Deliverables now show your own knowledge folder's name (hover for the full path), not RTM_PKM.
New Settings button (bottom left): choose Jarvis's voice and speed, his personality, colour themes (now saved for every browser), and the default model, including ChatGPT with your own OpenAI key.
The Jarvis shortcut now has its own icon instead of Python's.

If Claude Code isn't signed in on your computer, Jarvis now shows a Sign in card. Click Sign in, then Authorize in your browser, and you're done. Being signed in to the Claude desktop app doesn't sign in Claude Code, which Jarvis runs on.
Jarvis now always uses your own Claude sign-in, so it keeps working after a restart. If Claude Code isn't signed in, Jarvis tells you how to fix it instead of showing "Not logged in".
Setup can now keep Jarvis in its own folder and link it to a knowledge folder anywhere, OneDrive included.
Office: the CEO reads a book while nobody needs them, and now and then gets up for a workout in the new gym in front of the desk (treadmill, dumbbells, squat rack).
Office: when you deny a request, the CEO walks the paper to the Rejected bin at the front of the office and drops it in.
Updating once now brings in everything since your last update, and lists every change in one go.
Notes and deliverables now use the full width of the reader, and wide tables no longer get cut off.
Office: equipment names are now plates on the machines themselves, and the to-file paper piles sit at the front.
Office: a putting green beside Team HQ. Idle agents take turns, up to three putts each, and the team cheers a hole in one.
Open folder now shows the files in the main window: folders open in place, and files open with a click.
Creating a project now shows its progress, then opens the new project without the start screen.
Reloading the galaxy after the team rebuilds it no longer replays the start screen and greeting.
Ask Jarvis in your own words to open, close or filter things, such as "close everything and show me my week" or "what's overdue for Acme". Windows open in the middle of the screen.
New calendar window for any span: today, Friday, next week.
"Write me a document on..." has the team write it, and it opens on screen when finished.
Bot bubbles in Current work now show the task first, then the step, and no longer guess the wrong project.
The galaxy's clusters sit closer to the centre.
The galaxy's slow spin now circles your vault at the centre, not whatever you last clicked.
